pages.title: Need of Trie
pages.content:
Have you ever wondered how a search suggestion works, how a massive website like Google can look through billions of search strings, match them with the string typed by you and show you similar strings that might auto-complete your sentence, all in an instant. How a document editor can check the word typed by you against all the words in the dictionary in an instant to see if your spelling is correct or not?  

These operations and much more are done by a data structure called **Trie** and in this course you will learn all you need to know to implement and use tries yourself.

Operations of tries that you will learn in this course are:
- Insertion
- Search
- Deletion
- Print

### Applications of Trie
- Auto-Complete Systems
- Spell Checkers
- Prefix Matching
- Dictionary Implementations
- Text Compressions
- Genomic Sequence Analysis
- Routing Information Protocol
- Contact Management
- Word Games
- Compiler Design

practiceProblems.title: Structure of Trie
practiceProblems.description:
A Trie stores each word character by character. Each character is connected to others in a Tree like structure.

Each node has the following:
- An array of pointers where each index denotes a character which can be used in the string and each pointer points to the next node in the string.
- A Boolean which denotes the end of a string. When this value is true it means that one of the strings has completed.  



The following image shows a Trie containing the words ("call", "cat", "cats", "dog").

practiceProblems.title: Insertion in Trie
practiceProblems.description:
Steps to insert a word in trie: 
- We start at the root and set a variable current to the root.
- we iterate over the word and for each character ch in the word we:
    - get the index that represents that character
    - if that index of the children array does not contain a pointer to the next node we create a new trie node to save the pointer at that index.
    - we update the current variable to the next node.
- we set the end value of the current node to true.

Let's follow these steps to insert the word "cats" in the following trie:
```
      [ c     d ]
       /       \
     [a]       [o]
     /           \
  [ l  t ]       [g]
   /    \          \
 [l]    [end]   [end]
 /        
[end]     

```
- we set current = [c, d]
- we iterate on the word "cats"
    - ch = c , the index of c contains a pointer
    - we set current to the pointer at index of c
    - ch = a , the index of a contains a pointer
    - we set current to the pointer at index of a
    - ch = t , the index of t contains a pointer
    - we set current to the pointer at index of t
    - ch = s, the index of s does not contain a pointer
    - we create a new node and set the pointer denoting s to that new node
    - we set current to the new node
- we set the end of current node to true.

```
      [ c     d ]
       /       \
     [a]       [o]
     /           \
  [ l  t ]       [g]
   /    \          \
 [l]    [[s],end]  [end]
 /        \
[end]     [end]

```

Inspect the insert function in the code editor to see how to insert a word in a trie structure.

practiceProblems.title: Searching
practiceProblems.description:
Steps to if a word exists in a trie:  
- set a variable current and initialize it with root of the trie.
- iterate over the word to search in the trie.
    - update the current variable to the pointer stored in the children array at the position of the index of the character of the word.
- if the current node is not NULL and it's end is set to true then the word exists in the trie, else it doesn't exist in the trie.

Let's follow these steps to search if the word "cats" exists in the following trie:

```
      [ c     d ]
       /       \
     [a]       [o]
     /           \
  [ l  t ]       [g]
   /    \          \
 [l]    [[s],end]  [end]
 /        \
[end]     [end]

```
- the current is set to root.
- we iterate over the word cats.
    - ch = c, current = [c d], so we update current to the pointer stored at index of c.
    - ch = a, current = [a], so we update current to the pointer stored at index of a.
    - ch = t, current = [l t], so we update current to the pointer stored at index of t.
    - ch = s, current = [[s], end], we update the current to the pointer stored at index of s.
    - current = [end]
the end in the current is true, so the word exists in the trie.

Inspect the code editor to see how to search in the trie.

practiceProblems.title: Deletion
practiceProblems.description:
Steps to delete a word from a trie.
- Recursively traverse the trie to delete the given word.
- If the current node is nullptr, returns false (word not present in the trie).
- If the depth reaches the length of the word:
    - If the node is not an end-of-word node, returns false (word not present in the trie).
    - Sets the current node's isEndOfWord flag to false.
    - Checks if the current node has no children; if true, the node can be safely removed.
- Otherwise, continues the recursive deletion process for the next character in the word.
    - If the child node can be deleted, the child node is deleted, and its reference in the parent's children array is set to nullptr.
    - Checks if the current node has no children and is not an end-of-word node; if true, the node can be safely removed.

Let's follow these steps to delete the word "cats" from the following trie:
```
      [ c     d ]
       /       \
     [a]       [o]
     /           \
  [ l  t ]       [g]
   /    \          \
 [l]    [[s],end]  [end]
 /        \
[end]     [end]

```
- length = 4, depth = 0, current node = [c  d].
- length = 4, depth = 1, current node = [a].
- length = 4, depth = 2, current node = [l t].
- length = 4, depth = 3, current node = [[s], end].
- length = 4, depth = 4, current node = [end].
- Now the length == depth, so we check if it is the end of the word and if so we set it to false.
```
      [ c     d ]
       /       \
     [a]       [o]
     /           \
  [ l  t ]       [g]
   /    \          \
 [l]    [[s],end]  [end]
 /        \
[end]     []

```
- Now we backtrack, length = 4, depth = 3, current node = [[s], end].
- the pointer at s is replaced with nullptr, and if it's children can be deleted it is deleted.
```
      [ c     d ]
       /       \
     [a]       [o]
     /           \
  [ l  t ]       [g]
   /    \          \
 [l]    [end]     [end]
 /        
[end]     

```
- No other nodes can be deleted.
Inspect the code editor to see how to delete a word in the trie.

pages.title: Spell-Check MCQ
pages.content:
There exists a special dictionary with only specific words. These words are entered in a trie which is given below.
```
          [e         t]
          /         / \
        [i]       [h]  [w]
        /        /       \
      [g]      [r]       [o]
      /        /           \
    [h]     [e  o]        [end]
    /       /    \
  [t]     [e]     [n]
  /       /         \
[end]   [end]        [e]
                       \
                      [end]

```
Do the words trees and throne exist in this dictionary?

     [f______v]    [end]

    [e]       [e]

Rely on undocumented compiler behaviors and arbitrary memory pointers
Suppress error diagnostics and ignore unexpected input bounds
Execute unbounded linear searches across unsorted large-scale collections
questions.explanation: Engineering standards prioritize robustness, clear boundaries, and predictable time-space complexity.
